body:
## Problem

Another issue that i've been facing. a program running in `:terminal` is never told the window resized if it happens to be inside a synchronized update (mode 2026). it keeps 
drawing at the old size, then. causes some weird/slow visual updates for me


## Solution

report the new pty size even during a synchronized update

comment_data.diff_hunk:
@@ -114,6 +114,30 @@ describe(':terminal', function()
     ]])
   end)
 
+  it('forwards resize request during synchronized output (mode 2026)', function()
+    if is_os('win') then
+      pending('SIGWINCH is unreliable on Windows #7506')
+    end

IDTT there's a problem with the code, it just addresses a hypothetical circumstance that rarely occurs in practice.

AI findings:

> 
> `refresh_size()` is single-shot — it clears `term->pending.resize` and returns `true` exactly once.
> 
> Suggestion: Hoisting the call fixes that and removes the duplicated call site:
> 
> ```c
> bool resized = refresh_size(term);
> if (!term->synchronized_output) {
>   refresh_terminal(term, resized);
> }
> ```
> 
> Smaller things:
> 
> - `term->synchronized_output && !term->pending.resize` lets a resize flag decide whether *damage* is deferred. Until the timer fires (~10ms), every `invalidate_terminal()` bypasses the mode-2026 guard, and `terminal_destroy()` will then flush a half-finished frame through its `set_has(&invalidated_terminals, term)` path. A resize is just an ioctl to the pty — could it be flushed from `terminal_check_size()` rather than routed through the redraw queue (which also costs it 10ms of latency)?
> - `refresh_size()` returns early on `term->closed` without clearing `pending.resize`. Now that the flag gates deferral, a stuck flag disables mode-2026 deferral for that terminal permanently.
> - The new call site skips `refresh_terminal()`'s `handle_get_buffer()` / "Destroyed by `buf_freeall()`" check.
> - The comments above `invalidate_terminal()` and `refresh_timer_cb()` still describe the old behavior, and the rationale for the change (the program must learn the new size even mid-sync) isn't stated anywhere in the source.
> - Test: `\027[?2026h` round-trips through tty-test's stdin→stdout before vterm sets `synchronized_output`, so the three `sleep(100)`s aren't a guarantee.
>   - suggestion: A `screen:expect()` after each `try_resize`.  (`synchronized_output_spec.lua` already uses that pattern.)
>
I'm not going to push this forward, someone else can if they want to.
